newsitem.title: UK: US stocks mixed in London, Dow extends drop.
newsitem.headline: US stocks mixed in London, Dow extends drop.

text.p: U.S. shares were narrowly mixed in London on Tuesday in what dealers described as directionless activity.

Trading in Dow Chemical Co shares enlivened an otherwise dull market, as European investors sold the stock after news that a jury ruled against the company in the first U.S. class action lawsuit over breast implants.
The shares were quoted $1/2 lower at $88-1/2 in London, after shedding $2 in New York.
"We're still seeing some fallout from this suit," a London dealer said. "It went out very heavily offered last night."
Most technology shares firmed, led by Digital Equipment Corp, after the computer maker introduced two new notebook models of its HiNote Ultra 200 series. The shares were up $3/8 to $46.
International Business Machines Corp and Intel Corp shares each rose $1/2 to $104-1/2 and $95-1/16, respectively.
Most other U.S. stocks were trading within $1/8 of their closing levels in New York, dealers said.
"The market is directionless. I wouldn't even try to predict what will happen on Wall Street today," another dealer said.
The Federal Open Market Committee meeting starts today, although policy makers are expected to leave interest rates unchanged.
Figures on housing starts for July are set for release at 1230 GMT. July import and export price date are due at 1400 GMT.
On Globex, September S&P 500 futures were down 0.45 point to 918.30 at 1044 GMT, while September long bond futures were down 2/32 to 114-1/32.
The Dow rose 108.70 points to 7,803.36 on Monday.
